title: Assign Cookies
statement:
A teacher has `n` children and `m` cookies. Child `i` has a greed value `greed[i]`, and cookie `j` has a size `cookies[j]`.

A cookie can be given to a child only if **both** conditions hold:

- the cookie is big enough: `cookies[j] >= greed[i]`;
- the cookie and the child have the **same parity**: `cookies[j]` and `greed[i]` are both even or both odd.

Each child receives at most one cookie and each cookie is given to at most one child. A child who receives a cookie is content.

Return the maximum number of content children.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `m`.
The second line contains `n` integers `greed[0..n-1]`.
The third line contains `m` integers `cookies[0..m-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum number of children that can be made content.

examples.explanation: Only the child with greed 2 has the same parity as the available cookies (all even). One cookie is enough for that child, and the odd children cannot be served by any even cookie.
Even children (greed 2 and 4) are served by the even cookies 6 and 8. Odd children (greed 3 and 7) are served by the odd cookies 3 and 9. The spare cookie 3 is not needed.
Both children are odd, but every cookie is even, so nobody can be served despite the cookies being large.

complexity.time: O(n log n + m log m)

hints: The parity rule splits the problem in two: even children can only use even cookies and odd children can only use odd cookies.
Inside one parity class the rule is just 'cookie size >= greed'. Sort both sides.
Greedy: walk through the cookies from smallest to largest and give each cookie to the least greedy child who is still unserved, if that child accepts it.
